indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould anew, so the letters of the next word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor washed up on a beach is having a rough time of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast ashore' reads as shipwreck, but 'Cast' tells you to rearrange ASHORE; a voice that is rough is hoarse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, croaky voice is a harsh, husky one.

parts.note: a horn is a brass musical instrument
a pipe is a simple wind instrument

explanation.surface: A pair of instruments to accompany a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The hornpipe is a lively solo dance traditionally associated with sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornpipe is a lively sailors' dance, as well as the tune played for it.

indicators.note: fused means melted together, so these letters are melted down and recast

explanation.surface: A metal melted into many others in an alloy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fused' fits the metal picture but signals an anagram of INTO MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a brittle metalloid element, symbol Sb, used in alloys.

indicators.note: another version of the next word means its letters in a different order

explanation.surface: Dad gets a second pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' looks like a pay rise, but 'another' asks for a different arrangement of its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To sire is to beget, and as a noun it is a male parent, especially of a horse.

clue.text: I am getting stout as a business man

parts.note: contracted, I am is I'm
porter is a dark beer closely related to stout

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that drinking stout befits a businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like a description of a portly person, but it is the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who brings goods in from abroad is a kind of merchant.

parts.note: fulfilling promise suggests realising potential, but it means keeping one's pledges

explanation.surface: A young talent who will live up to expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a person who reliably keeps every undertaking he makes.

clue.text: Party rising in power in old Scandinavia

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political party gaining influence in historic Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party rising in power' reads as political success, but 'rising' turns DO into OD; then IN follows and 'power' begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin was the chief god of Norse mythology, a deity worshipped by the Vikings.

clue.text: Signs liable to be kicked over

explanation.surface: Clues that someone might upset.
explanation.walkthrough: To kick over the traces, the straps joining a horse to its cart, is to throw off restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestiges or marks are signs left behind, and harness straps are what a restive horse kicks over.

clue.text: Hemp is used in making this jacket

definitions.text: Hemp is used in making this jacket

parts.words: Hemp is used in making this jacket
parts.note: hemp reads as the fabric of a coat, but the drug cannabis rolled into a cigarette shares the coat's name

explanation.surface: A coat woven from hemp fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-breasted sailor's coat and a cannabis cigarette share this name.

clue.text: A quick reply from the laboratory?

explanation.surface: A witty comeback straight out of a science lab.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp riposte is a comeback, and a long-necked glass vessel for distilling is a chemistry flask of the same name.

indicators.note: variety suggests a mixture or assortment, so these letters come in a different order

explanation.surface: A performer recalls appearing in a music-hall variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety show' looks like one phrase, but 'variety' is the anagram signal on I ACTED IN and 'show' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to point it out or signal it.

clue.text: A friend at the gathering appears timorous

indicators.note: a gathering brings things together in a fresh arrangement, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A pal at the party seems shy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the gathering' reads as a social setting, but 'gathering' signals an anagram of A FRIEND AT THE; 'appears' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Timorous people are timid and lacking in courage.

explanation.surface: Asking what really drives rising prices.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone persistently is to grill them for information, and a tyre or balloon inflator blows air in.

indicators.note: read as out right, it tells you to remove the letter R, the usual abbreviation for right

parts.note: a gaffer is a foreman or boss of a work gang

explanation.surface: A works supervisor has made a complete mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outright' looks like 'utter', but split it as 'out R': the R for right leaves GAFFER.
explanation.definitionFit: A social slip or embarrassing mistake is a faux pas.

parts.note: mi or me is the third note of the sol-fa scale
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Gauging a pair of musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To dole out or allot in portions is to measure out.

explanation.surface: A jewel with a guaranteed weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewel is a precious stone, and in British imperial units a stone is a weight of fourteen pounds.

clue.text: Rambling tour including river and town in Cornwall

indicators.note: including means one piece is taken inside the other
rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so these letters stray into a new order

parts.note: R is a common abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A walking tour of the countryside takes in a river and a Cornish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' turns TOUR into TURO and 'including' puts R inside it. Cornwall is the county at England's south-west tip, and Truro is its cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Truro is the administrative centre and only city of Cornwall.

clue.text: Where you might go in America if you have time

definitions.text: Where you might go in America if you have time

parts.words: Where you might go in America if you have time
parts.note: having time reads as having leisure, but it means serving a prison sentence in the United States

explanation.surface: A suggestion for a destination when on holiday in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: An American state prison is where convicts serving time are held.

clue.text: You shouldn't miss this store opening

explanation.surface: A shop launch not to be missed.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone who couldn't hit a barn door is a poor shot; the barn is the store.
explanation.definitionFit: The big entrance to a farm building is proverbially too large a target to miss.

parts.note: stock-holder reads as a shareholder, but the stock is the handle of a whip held by a rider

explanation.surface: Controlling interest belonging to a shareholder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the upper hand, from the hand a rider holds the riding crop in.

parts.note: bound reads as obliged, but it means heading somewhere, as in homeward bound, while ready for battle

explanation.surface: Someone who is obliged to get into a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone angrily seeking a confrontation, from Native American war parties setting out.

clue.text: V-sign shows one is not in agreement!

parts.note: Aries the ram is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Flicking a V-sign shows someone disagrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'V-sign' looks like the rude gesture, but it is V followed by a zodiac sign; 'shows one' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To differ from something or diverge is to disagree with it.

explanation.surface: A beast that people drive about.
explanation.definitionFit: A big spotted wild cat of the Americas is also a British luxury car marque.

clue.text: The first man to be a father-and a mother

definitions.text: The first man to be a father

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: The original man became both a dad and a mum.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible the first man was also the first father; 'and' joins the definition to the wordplay, A plus DAM, the word for an animal's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first human created had sons Cain and Abel, so he was the first father.

indicators.note: round means placed around another piece

parts.note: lard is pig fat
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A portly Scotsman is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One fat round' reads as a stout man, but 'round' puts LARD round I. A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a landed proprietor in Scotland, so he is a Scot.

clue.text: Game in which all matches are exciting

definitions.text: Game in which all matches are exciting

parts.words: Game in which all matches are exciting
parts.note: matches reads as contests, but in this card game a matching pair of cards triggers a shout

explanation.surface: A sport where every fixture is thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: In this children's card game, players call out when two turned-up cards are the same.

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister's lovely garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister 1955-57; the biblical garden is Paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Anthony was a postwar British premier, and Genesis names the paradise of Adam and Eve so.

clue.text: Actors, and what they want to be

explanation.surface: Performers and their ambitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The performers in a play are its company, and every actor hopes to be chosen for a part.

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters of the two names are tossed about

explanation.surface: A relative called Enid is struggling in a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floundering' fits the swamp picture, but it signals the anagram of AUNT ENID.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp something is to flood or overwhelm it.

clue.text: Knock out some facts about aircraft

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: data are facts and figures
KO is the boxing abbreviation for knockout

explanation.surface: Some striking information about planes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'concerning' but puts DATA around KO. The Douglas Dakota was a famous transport plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douglas DC-3 transport plane was known in RAF service by this name.

clue.text: Song composed about the present time

indicators.note: about means one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: serene means calm and composed
AD, anno domini, marks the current era

explanation.surface: A piece of music written about modern times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like 'written', but it is the adjective, calm: SERENE goes about AD.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening love song sung under a window is a classic piece of music.

indicators.note: sorted out suggests something rearranged, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Things tidied and filed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted out' reads as tidied, but 'out' signals rearranging SORTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept in reserve has been put by for later.
